liability.data: The values shown here come from what was entered into the system. Accuracy, completeness and currency of the data are the user's responsibility alone.
liability.calculation: The calculation is an arithmetic summary of the amounts and days that were entered. It does not determine entitlements or payment rates and is not a substitute for a payslip or for review by a professional.
liability.forecast: The forecast projects the entered data forward and does not account for changes in rates, entitlements or circumstances. It is a planning estimate only and is not financial advice.
liability.score: The score is not a substitute for independent checking or professional advice, and it does not guarantee that no obligations or deadlines remain open.
liability.reminder: Dates and alerts are calculated from the dates that were entered. Delivery of any alert is not guaranteed, and tracking and meeting the deadlines remains the user's responsibility.

input.label: Entered
input.meaning: A value entered by the user. The system does not verify it and asserts nothing about it.

calculated.label: Calculated
calculated.meaning: A value the system derived by a formula from entered values. It is not legal truth and it is not a payslip.

paid.label: Paid
paid.meaning: A value recorded as a payment that was actually made, according to what was reported to the system.

forecast.label: Forecast
forecast.meaning: A projection about the future. It is not a fact and it is not a payment that was made.

valueOrigin.legendTitle: How to read the numbers here
valueOrigin.legendIntro: Every amount carries a label saying what it is: entered values are the user's responsibility, calculated values are derived from entered data, paid values are recorded as payments that were made, and a forecast is an estimate only.

guidePage.kicker: A practical guide for employing families
guidePage.title: Direct caregiver employment — what should you manage?
guidePage.intro: Direct employment involves several parallel processes. An organized list, clear dates and consistent records make it easier to see what is complete and what still needs attention.
guidePage.section1Title: 1. Employment details and the people involved
guidePage.section1Body: Start with employer, care recipient and caregiver details, the employment start date and an authorized contact. The rest of the system relies on this information.
guidePage.section2Body: Record each document's name, type, expiry date and current status. An early reminder helps start renewal work before expiry but does not replace checking with the relevant authority.
guidePage.section3Body: Record policy periods and align tracking with the employment start date. Before changes or renewals, verify coverage requirements with the insurer or another qualified source.
guidePage.section4Body: A clear monthly record separates base pay, Saturdays or rest days, additions and deductions. Saved summaries create an annual record and a clear copy for employer and caregiver, but do not replace professional review.
guidePage.section5Body: Organize monthly, quarterly and annual tasks by opening and deadline dates. This distinguishes tasks that are not open yet, open tasks and items that need attention.
guidePage.noticeBody: Rules, rates and deadlines can change. CareDesk helps organize and document; verify information with an official source or qualified professional before financial or legal action.
guidePage.ctaTitle: Want to turn the list into a workflow?
guidePage.ctaBody: CareDesk presents information in short screens with tasks, reminders and summaries.

terms.section1Body: CareDesk is operated by [שם בעל העסק — להשלמה], a sole trader, business number 056543507 (the "Operator"). Postal address: [כתובת לפניות — להשלמה]. Enquiries on any matter arising from these terms: boaz.nachshony@gmail.com.

terms.section4Title: 4. What the service is, and what it is not
terms.section4Body: CareDesk is a tool for organising, recording and being reminded about the direct employment of a live-in caregiver. It brings together documents, dates, payroll records and medication records, and derives from them calculations, scores, forecasts and alerts. Those outputs are derived from the data entered and are aids only: they are not legal, accounting, medical or financial advice, they do not determine entitlements or rates of pay, and they are not a substitute for a payslip, an official filing or a review by a qualified professional. The Operator does not verify any figure against an external register and does not fill in missing data. privacy.title: CareDesk privacy policy
privacy.updated: Version {{version}} — a professional draft pending review by a lawyer before it is published as a binding document.
privacy.intro: This document explains what data the service collects, who holds it, where it is stored, and how it can be accessed, corrected and deleted. It speaks in particular to the situation unique to this service: the account holder enters information about another person — the caregiver.
privacy.section1Title: 1. Who we are and what this document covers
privacy.section1Body: Data is collected and processed by [שם בעל העסק — להשלמה], a sole trader, business number 056543507 (the "Operator"). Postal address: [כתובת לפניות — להשלמה]. Privacy enquiries: boaz.nachshony@gmail.com. This policy applies to the CareDesk service and its public site and forms an integral part of the terms of service.
privacy.section2Body: a. Account data — name, email address and sign-in details of the account holder and of authorised users. b. Billing data — name and email address for invoicing and transaction identifiers. The card number and CVV are not collected and are not stored by the Operator; they are entered directly with the payment processor. c. Care recipient and household data — name, contact details, address and dates. d. Caregiver data — name, contact details, nationality, passport or identity number, visa and employment-permit data and their expiry dates, and scanned identity documents uploaded to the service. e. Employment and payroll data — base salary, rest days, deductions, payment records and payroll documents. f. Medication records entered for reminder purposes — information that is health data in nature. g. Technical usage data — error logs, request identifiers and audit records, used for operations, security and fault diagnosis. The service runs no advertising, behavioural analytics or cross-site tracking.
privacy.section3Title: 3. Caregiver data and identity documents — the account holder's responsibility
privacy.section3Body: The most sensitive part of the data in the service is not information about the account holder but about another person: the caregiver. The account holder is the one who enters it, and the account holder — not the Operator — is responsible for having a lawful basis to hold it and to enter it into the service, including informing the caregiver that the data is held and for what purpose, and obtaining her consent where the law requires it. Identity documents or data of a person the account holder has no lawful basis to hold must not be uploaded. We recommend telling the caregiver that her details and documents are managed in this service and allowing her to review them.
privacy.section4Body: Holding the data of the account holder and of authorised users rests on their consent and on the necessity of performing the engagement between them and the Operator. Acceptance of the terms and of this policy is recorded: the system stores who accepted, which document, which version and when, and does not permit that record to be altered after the fact. Holding the caregiver's data rests on the lawful basis held by the account holder, as set out in section 3; the Operator holds it for the account holder and on their instructions. Processing for billing, security and compliance also takes place where it is required to meet a legal obligation of the Operator.
privacy.section5Body: The account holder owns the data entered into their account. The Operator is its holder and processes it for the account holder and on their instructions only, and does not use it for any other purpose. The data is not sold, rented or transferred to any third party for marketing. Transfer to a third party occurs only to the suppliers listed in section 6 for the purpose of providing the service, or where required by law, court order or the demand of a competent authority.
privacy.section6Title: 6. Sub-processors and where data is stored
privacy.section6Body: The service is delivered using suppliers acting as sub-processors: Supabase — database, identity management and file storage; Vercel — application and API hosting; Cardcom — payment-method processing and invoicing; Resend — sending email from the service. The database and file storage are located in the Frankfurt region, Germany, within the European Union. Card details are held by the payment processor in Israel and never pass through the Operator's servers. The list of sub-processors may be updated; a material update will be notified in advance as set out in section 11.
privacy.section7Body: Traffic to and from the service is encrypted with TLS. Data is encrypted at rest: database and file storage are encrypted at the infrastructure layer, and in addition sensitive workspace fields are encrypted at the application layer under a dedicated, rotatable key. Separation between customers is enforced in the database itself (row level security), so that a request made by one account cannot return another account's data. Documents are reached only through short-lived links, and authorised users' permissions are set by the account holder. Sensitive operations are written to an audit log.
privacy.section8Body: Account data is retained for as long as the subscription is live. Cancelling the subscription stops billing and does not delete data. Deletion is carried out at the account holder's request to the address in section 11, following identity verification; once the request is approved, account data and files are deleted within 30 days. Excepted from this is data the Operator is required by law to retain — including accounting records and invoices, kept for the period the law prescribes — and audit records and the records of acceptance of the legal documents, kept as evidence of the engagement. Backups are retained for a limited period and are removed in the ordinary backup cycle.
privacy.section9Body: Under the Israeli Privacy Protection Law, 5741-1981 and its regulations, every person is entitled to inspect information held about them in a database and to request the correction of information that is inaccurate, incomplete, unclear or out of date. Requests for access or correction should be sent to boaz.nachshony@gmail.com and will be answered within the periods the law prescribes. The account holder can inspect and correct their account data directly in the service. A request for access or correction made by the caregiver will be passed to the account holder, who owns the data, and the Operator will provide technical assistance alongside. A refusal of an access or correction request will be given in writing with reasons and may be challenged as provided by law.
privacy.section10Body: If a serious security incident affecting data held in the service comes to light, the affected account holder will be notified without unreasonable delay and in any event within 72 hours of the Operator becoming aware of it. The notice will describe the nature of the incident, the categories of data exposed so far as known, the steps taken and the recommended protective measures. Notification to the Israeli Privacy Protection Authority will be made as the law requires. Suspected security incidents or vulnerabilities in the service should be reported to boaz.nachshony@gmail.com.
privacy.section11Title: 11. Changes to this policy and contact
privacy.section11Body: The Operator may update this policy. A material change — including a change to the purposes of use, to the identity of the sub-processors or to where data is stored — will be notified to the account holder by email and in the service at least 30 days in advance. The policy version and its date appear at the top of this page; the version accepted and the moment of acceptance are recorded and retained. Privacy enquiries: boaz.nachshony@gmail.com. Postal address: [כתובת לפניות — להשלמה].
privacy.legalNotice: This document describes the policy in practice and is not legal advice. Where it conflicts with a mandatory provision of law, the law prevails.
